- [IRET.1.4] **Interned strings (refcounted fact-slot values).**
  The per-engine string table holds two entry classes in one
  pointer space: **pinned** — schema/slot/rule names and
  compile-time literals, interned at load, engine-lifetime,
  never freed; and **counted** — `String`/`Bytes` slot values,
  reference-counted by the number of live committed fact slots
  holding the string and freed when the last such slot
  retracts. Four operations: `find` (non-mutating lookup, for
  no-op / dedup), `acquire` (find-or-insert + refcount++, once
  per `String`/`Bytes` slot at fact commit), `release`
  (refcount--, free + remove at 0, once per slot at fact
  retract), `pin` (insert saturated). The open-addressing table
  supports deletion (tombstones) so a freed counted entry is
  reclaimed. A value equal to a pinned literal shares the
  literal's pointer (stays pinned).

  Every other dynamic string the engine **computes** but does
  not store in a fact slot — an interpolated string, `gensym`, `json`→string, `cache-get` value,
  `where`-predicate operands — is **never interned**: it lives
  in a fire-scoped bump arena ([IRET.1.4a]) and is copied into a
  counted entry only if it is emitted into a fact slot. This
  bounds the table to live facts + structural vocabulary (seals
  SI1 oversized-at-destroy and SI2 unbounded computed-string
  growth).

  Rete **structural** comparisons (alpha EQ/NEQ, beta join,
  identity hash / equal) stay pointer-equality: they only ever
  see stored (interned) slot values, and equal stored strings
  still share one pointer. **Eval-level** `==` / `<` / `>` on
  strings is a length-aware **content** comparison — a computed
  arena operand is not interned, so an equal-content value has a
  different pointer and must still compare equal (and content
  order is deterministic, unlike pointer order).
